name: Zul'Gurub
summary: In northeastern Stranglethorn Vale, Zul'Gurub's jungle trolls scheme to summon an ancient entity into the world. The ruined temple city once stood at the heart of the Gurubashi Empire.

sections.title: Heart of the Fallen Empire
sections.body:
Thousands of years ago, Zul'Gurub was the vibrant capital of the Gurubashi Empire. Its stone ziggurats rose over a realm united under Gurubashi rule. Then civil war came, roughly fifteen hundred years before the Dark Portal opened.

The Atal'ai, a radical sect of priests, tried to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer and claim absolute power. Loyalist tribes joined forces and defeated them. The Atal'ai were banished north to the Swamp of Sorrows. The war broke the empire, and Zul'Gurub became a violent shadow of its former grandeur.

sections.title: The Looming Shadow of the Soulflayer
sections.body:
The fanatical worshippers of Hakkar kept their devotion after exile. They learned that his physical avatar could be summoned only from Zul'Gurub, his ancient ritual seat. Within the city, dark sorcerers such as Jin'do the Hexxer have sought to enslave Gurubashi high priests for blood rituals in Hakkar's name.

Hyper-aggressive Gurubashi trolls prowl the jungle around the ruins, driven into a murderous frenzy. Zul'Gurub remains an epicenter of dread for anyone who ventures near its borders.

faq.answer: Zul'Gurub is an ancient temple city in northeastern Stranglethorn Vale. Thousands of years ago, it was the vibrant capital of the Gurubashi Empire. Now the ruined city is a dangerous stronghold inhabited by hostile Gurubashi trolls.
Hakkar the Soulflayer is an ancient, terrible blood god. The fanatical Atal'ai worship him, and his cultists have long plotted to bring his physical avatar into Azeroth through rituals in Zul'Gurub.

faq.q: Why did the Gurubashi Empire collapse?
faq.answer: Roughly fifteen hundred years before the Dark Portal opened, civil war tore the Gurubashi Empire apart. The radical Atal'ai priests tried to summon Hakkar. The other trolls defeated and banished them, but the war left the empire shattered.

faq.q: Can adventurers safely explore the ruins?
faq.answer: No. Zul'Gurub is exceptionally hazardous. The trolls in its ruins are violently aggressive and driven by bloody fervor. Treasure hunters and artifact seekers regularly disappear within its stone walls, and very few return.

angles.text: For the Darkspear tribe, Zul'Gurub is a monument to their ancestors' fallen grandeur and a warning of the ruinous price of serving Hakkar.
The Horde watches Zul'Gurub's dark rituals warily. Hakkar's return threatens nearby settlements and tribes across Stranglethorn.
